turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Owen found out about the zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me. I have twenty minutes before a client call. Start with who decided, and when.
The checker said 94 percent. That's the end of it.

"The end of it." Your own procedure, 4.3, says software doesn't establish a concern by itself, and the company that sells it says the same thing, and I have that page in my bag. So I'll ask again: who decided, and did anyone hear Owen first?
I don't need more proof than that.
"Don't need more proof." I'm writing that down, word for word. Withdraw the zero today, or I'm in the principal's office before you've packed up.
The software doesn't lie, unlike some people.
Owen doesn't lie, and I'd like you to finish that sentence: unlike whom? Are you calling my son a liar, or me? Choose carefully, because it's going into my notes either way.

Then you've heard Owen's side never, called me never, and decided on a machine's guess. I'm going to the principal's office from here, and after that the board under section 42. Last chance, Hale: is there anything else, or is that your whole case?
